text:
Recent work supports separating sequential transitions from general item similarity. MQSA-TED (WSDM 2024) combines short/long attention queries with distillation of global item-to-item transitions into embeddings—an applicable extension to SASRec without pretrained text models ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.01056)). *Revisiting Graph Projections* (2025) offers a simpler alternative: infer complementary recommendations using a directed, weighted item graph projected from historical user–item interactions, explicitly addressing sparse, noisy observations ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09209)). Earlier SCG-SPRe explicitly models substitutable and complementary relations separately, providing architectural precedent for distinct relation channels ([paper](https://doi.org/10.1145/3464302)). These results motivate directional scoring, but observed transitions alone do not establish functional complementarity.

Text-aware work also warns against treating semantic similarity as sufficient: ST2SI (COLING 2025) emphasizes learning item transitions and aligning text with item IDs; its pretrained-LLM implementation falls outside this task’s constraints ([paper](https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.171/)). A lightweight experimental adaptation—not a reported result—would blend SASRec scores with a smoothed, recency-weighted directed transition graph, using separate source/target embeddings to preserve asymmetry. Locally fitted title/description TF-IDF/SVD features or randomly initialized token embeddings could share statistical strength across sparse items; train distinct projections for transition prediction and semantic similarity rather than declaring similar items complementary. Construct all graph counts and text representations from permitted training data, retain category routing, and select graph/text mixing weights using macro validation HR@10. Treat this as next-item prediction: basket-specific assumptions require observed basket boundaries.
